out.answers: The question of who should pay for higher education has long been a matter of debate While I accept that cost should never prevent talented young people from studying I do not believe that university should be completely free for everyone It is undeniable that free tuition would bring certain benefits Students from low-income families would no longer be deterred by high fees or graduate with crippling debts and society as a whole would gain from a more highly skilled workforce For instance several Nordic countries offer tuition-free degrees and they consistently rank among the best-educated nations in the world However making higher education free for all would place an enormous burden on public finances The money would have to come from taxes which means that ordinary workers many of whom never attended university would be subsidising graduates who are likely to earn higher salaries later in life Moreover when governments must fund unlimited places universities often suffer from overcrowded lecture halls and a decline in teaching quality In some countries that abolished fees class sizes grew so quickly that students struggled to receive individual attention from their lecturers A fairer approach would be to combine modest fees with generous financial support Means-tested grants and scholarships could cover the full cost for students from disadvantaged backgrounds while income-contingent loans would require graduates to repay only once they earn above a certain threshold In this way access would be determined by ability rather than wealth In conclusion although free university education appears attractive at first glance I believe that a targeted system of financial aid is a more sustainable and equitable solution as it protects both opportunity and public finances

issues.q: Should university education be free for all students?

for.vi: Học phí miễn phí giúp sinh viên nghèo có cơ hội học đại học như sinh viên khá giả, giảm bất bình đẳng xã hội.

chunks: widen access to higher education|mở rộng cơ hội học đại học
regardless of financial background|bất kể hoàn cảnh tài chính

for.vi: Lực lượng lao động có trình độ cao hơn sẽ thúc đẩy năng suất, đổi mới và tăng trưởng kinh tế.
for.ex: Countries such as Germany, which offer free degrees, benefit from a highly skilled workforce that drives innovation in engineering, medicine and technology.
chunks: a highly skilled workforce|lực lượng lao động tay nghề cao
drive economic growth|thúc đẩy tăng trưởng kinh tế

for.vi: Sinh viên ra trường không phải gánh khoản nợ lớn, nên có thể chọn nghề theo đam mê thay vì chỉ vì lương.
for.ex: Without huge student loans, graduates can choose careers they are passionate about, such as teaching or social work, rather than chasing the highest salary.
chunks: be saddled with debt|gánh nặng nợ nần
pursue a career of their choice|theo đuổi nghề nghiệp mình chọn

against.ex: Funding free degrees would force governments to raise taxes, meaning that factory workers who never attended university would pay for the education of future doctors and lawyers.
chunks: place a burden on taxpayers|đặt gánh nặng lên người nộp thuế
divert funds from|rút bớt ngân sách khỏi

against.vi: Khi số sinh viên tăng mà ngân sách có hạn, lớp học đông hơn và chất lượng đào tạo có thể giảm.

chunks: overcrowded lecture halls|giảng đường quá tải
compromise the quality of teaching|làm giảm chất lượng giảng dạy

against.vi: Người có bằng đại học thường có thu nhập cao hơn, nên việc họ tự đóng góp một phần chi phí là công bằng.

<<Mở bài>> The line graph [[illustrates|minh họa]] [[the proportion of households|tỉ lệ hộ gia đình]] in a European country that relied on gas, electricity and renewable sources [[for heating|để sưởi ấm]] [[over the thirty-year period from 1990 to 2020|trong giai đoạn 30 năm từ 1990 đến 2020]].

<<Tổng quan>> {{Overall}}, gas [[remained the dominant heating source|vẫn là nguồn sưởi chủ đạo]] throughout the period, {{although}} its share [[declined steadily|giảm đều đặn]]. {{By contrast}}, renewables [[saw a dramatic increase|có sự gia tăng đáng kể]] and had [[almost caught up with|gần như bắt kịp]] gas by the final year.

<<Thân bài 1>> In 1990, gas was used by 62% of households, [[well ahead of|bỏ xa]] electricity at 25%, {{while}} renewables [[accounted for a mere|chỉ chiếm vỏn vẹn]] 3%. The figure for gas [[edged up to a peak of|nhích lên đạt đỉnh]] 64% in 1995 {{but}} then [[fell continuously|giảm liên tục]], reaching just 35% in 2020. Electricity [[followed a gradual upward trend|đi theo xu hướng tăng dần]], rising from 24% in 1995 to 34% in 2015 before [[levelling off|chững lại]] at 33%.

<<Thân bài 2>> {{Meanwhile}}, the use of renewable energy grew slowly at first, reaching only 6% in 2000. {{However}}, [[growth accelerated considerably|tốc độ tăng trưởng tăng mạnh]] [[in the following two decades|trong hai thập kỷ sau đó]], with the proportion climbing to 15% in 2010 and 31% in 2020. {{As a result}}, renewables [[were only two percentage points behind|chỉ kém hai điểm phần trăm so với]] electricity in the final year and [[trailed gas by just|chỉ thua gas]] four points.

<<Mở bài>> The bar chart [[compares the average amount of time|so sánh lượng thời gian trung bình]] that people in four age groups [[spent each week on|dành mỗi tuần cho]] social media, sport and reading in 2022.

<<Tổng quan>> {{Overall}}, time spent on social media [[was inversely related to age|tỉ lệ nghịch với tuổi tác]], {{whereas}} the opposite was true for reading. Young people [[devoted far more time to|dành nhiều thời gian hơn hẳn cho]] social media than to any other activity, {{while}} reading was [[the most popular pastime|thú vui phổ biến nhất]] among those aged 65 and over.

<<Thân bài 1>> Those aged 16 to 24 spent 14 hours a week on social media, [[more than double the figure for|gấp hơn hai lần con số của]] sport (6 hours) and seven times as much as reading (2 hours). Time spent online [[dropped sharply with age|giảm mạnh theo độ tuổi]], [[falling to|giảm xuống còn]] 9 hours for the 25–44 group, 5 hours for people aged 45 to 64 and [[a mere two hours|chỉ vỏn vẹn hai giờ]] for the oldest group.

<<Thân bài 2>> Reading [[showed the reverse pattern|thể hiện xu hướng ngược lại]], rising from 2 hours among the youngest respondents to 8 hours among the over-65s, [[making it|khiến nó trở thành]] their main leisure activity. In the 45–64 group, reading and social media [[were equally popular|phổ biến như nhau]], at 5 hours each. Sport, {{meanwhile}}, [[varied relatively little|dao động tương đối ít]] [[across the age groups|giữa các nhóm tuổi]], ranging from 3 to 6 hours, {{although}} it was [[slightly more popular|phổ biến hơn một chút]] among the oldest people (4 hours) than among the 45–64 group (3 hours).

<<Mở bài>> [[The question of who should pay for higher education|Vấn đề ai nên chi trả cho giáo dục đại học]] [[has long been a matter of debate|từ lâu đã là chủ đề tranh luận]]. {{While}} I accept that [[cost should never prevent|chi phí không bao giờ nên ngăn cản]] talented young people from studying, I do not believe that university should be completely free for everyone.

<<Thân bài 1>> <<Nhượng bộ>> [[It is undeniable that|Không thể phủ nhận rằng]] free tuition [[would bring certain benefits|sẽ mang lại một số lợi ích]]. <<Giải thích>> Students from low-income families would no longer [[be deterred by|bị cản bước bởi]] high fees or [[graduate with crippling debts|tốt nghiệp với khoản nợ nặng nề]], and society as a whole [[would gain from|sẽ được hưởng lợi từ]] a more highly skilled workforce. <<Ví dụ>> {{For instance}}, several Nordic countries [[offer tuition-free degrees|cung cấp bằng đại học miễn học phí]], and they [[consistently rank among|liên tục nằm trong nhóm]] the best-educated nations in the world.

<<Thân bài 2>> <<Câu chủ đề>> {{However}}, [[making higher education free for all|việc miễn phí giáo dục đại học cho tất cả]] [[would place an enormous burden on|sẽ đặt gánh nặng khổng lồ lên]] public finances. <<Giải thích>> The money would have to come from taxes, which means that [[ordinary workers|người lao động bình thường]], many of whom never attended university, would be [[subsidising graduates|trợ cấp cho người có bằng đại học]] who are likely to [[earn higher salaries|có mức lương cao hơn]] later in life. {{Moreover}}, when governments must fund unlimited places, universities often [[suffer from|chịu cảnh]] overcrowded lecture halls and [[a decline in teaching quality|chất lượng giảng dạy đi xuống]]. <<Ví dụ>> In some countries that abolished fees, class sizes grew so quickly that students struggled to receive [[individual attention|sự quan tâm riêng]] from their lecturers.

<<Thân bài 3>> <<Câu chủ đề>> [[A fairer approach|Một cách tiếp cận công bằng hơn]] would be to [[combine modest fees with|kết hợp mức học phí vừa phải với]] generous financial support. <<Giải thích>> Means-tested grants and scholarships could [[cover the full cost|chi trả toàn bộ chi phí]] for students from disadvantaged backgrounds, {{while}} income-contingent loans would [[require graduates to repay|yêu cầu người tốt nghiệp hoàn trả]] only once they earn above a certain threshold. {{In this way}}, [[access would be determined by ability rather than wealth|cơ hội được quyết định bởi năng lực thay vì sự giàu có]].

<<Kết bài>> {{In conclusion}}, {{although}} free university education [[appears attractive|có vẻ hấp dẫn]] [[at first glance|thoạt nhìn]], I believe that [[a targeted system of financial aid|hệ thống hỗ trợ tài chính có trọng tâm]] is [[a more sustainable and equitable solution|giải pháp bền vững và công bằng hơn]], as it protects both opportunity and public finances.

<<Mở bài>> [[In recent years|Trong những năm gần đây]], [[the effects of climate change|tác động của biến đổi khí hậu]] have led some people to argue that environmental protection should [[receive a larger share of|nhận phần lớn hơn của]] public funding than any other service. {{Although}} I agree that environmental spending must increase, I disagree that it should [[take priority over|được ưu tiên hơn]] essential services such as healthcare and education.

<<Thân bài 1>> <<Nhượng bộ>> [[There is no doubt that|Không còn nghi ngờ gì rằng]] environmental problems [[pose a serious threat to|gây ra mối đe dọa nghiêm trọng cho]] human well-being. <<Giải thích>> Floods, droughts and air pollution [[cause enormous economic losses|gây thiệt hại kinh tế khổng lồ]] and [[put pressure on|gây áp lực lên]] other public services, {{especially}} hospitals. <<Ví dụ>> {{For example}}, a city that invests in flood defences today may [[save far more|tiết kiệm được nhiều hơn hẳn]] in reconstruction costs [[in the long run|về lâu dài]].

<<Thân bài 2>> <<Câu chủ đề>> {{Nevertheless}}, [[it would be unwise to|sẽ là thiếu khôn ngoan nếu]] [[divert funds away from|chuyển hướng ngân sách khỏi]] services that people [[depend on daily|phụ thuộc hằng ngày]]. <<Giải thích>> Governments [[have a fundamental duty to|có nghĩa vụ cơ bản là]] keep citizens healthy, educated and safe, and [[cutting budgets in these areas|cắt giảm ngân sách ở những lĩnh vực này]] would harm the most vulnerable groups first. <<Ví dụ>> A patient waiting for urgent surgery or a child in an underfunded school [[cannot afford to wait|không thể chờ đợi được]] while money is spent on long-term environmental projects.

<<Thân bài 3>> <<Câu chủ đề>> {{Furthermore}}, environmental protection [[does not have to compete with|không nhất thiết phải cạnh tranh với]] other services. <<Giải thích>> Many green policies, such as [[improving public transport|cải thiện giao thông công cộng]] or [[insulating schools and hospitals|cách nhiệt trường học và bệnh viện]], [[serve several goals at once|phục vụ nhiều mục tiêu cùng lúc]]. {{In addition}}, measures like carbon taxes can [[generate revenue|tạo ra nguồn thu]] rather than consume it. <<Ví dụ>> {{For instance}}, revenue from such taxes could be [[reinvested in|tái đầu tư vào]] hospitals or schools, [[benefiting both|mang lại lợi ích cho cả]] the environment and society.

<<Kết bài>> {{In conclusion}}, {{while}} the environment clearly deserves greater investment, I believe that [[a balanced approach|một cách tiếp cận cân bằng]] which [[integrates environmental goals into|lồng ghép mục tiêu môi trường vào]] all areas of public spending is far more effective than [[placing it above|đặt nó lên trên]] everything else.

<<Lời chào>> Dear Sir or Madam,

<<Mục đích thư>> I am writing to [[express my dissatisfaction with|bày tỏ sự không hài lòng về]] a washing machine I recently purchased from your website.

<<Ý 1>> I placed the order on 3 March, and the machine, a Zenith 8 kg front-loader, was delivered five days later. The order number is ZN40217, and I paid £429 by credit card.

<<Ý 2>> {{Unfortunately}}, the machine has [[not worked properly since the day it arrived|chưa hoạt động bình thường kể từ ngày được giao]]. The drum stops spinning halfway through every cycle, {{so}} my clothes come out soaking wet. {{In addition}}, water [[leaks onto the kitchen floor|rò rỉ ra sàn bếp]] each time I use it. I have followed the instructions carefully, so I am confident that [[the fault lies with the machine itself|lỗi nằm ở chính chiếc máy]].

<<Ý 3>> I would be grateful if you could [[arrange for the machine to be collected|sắp xếp đến thu hồi chiếc máy]] and replaced with a new one [[as soon as possible|càng sớm càng tốt]]. {{Alternatively}}, I would accept [[a full refund|hoàn tiền toàn bộ]].

<<Kết thư>> Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to [[hearing from you at your earliest convenience|nhận được hồi âm sớm nhất có thể]].

Yours faithfully,
Lan Nguyen

<<Lời chào>> Dear Sir or Madam,

<<Mục đích thư>> I am writing to [[apply for the position of|ứng tuyển vào vị trí]] part-time weekend guide at the City History Museum.

<<Ý 1>> I [[came across your advertisement|tình cờ thấy thông báo tuyển dụng của quý bảo tàng]] on the noticeboard at the central library last week, and I was delighted to see that you are looking for new staff.

<<Ý 2>> I am currently in my final year of a history degree, {{so}} I have [[a thorough knowledge of|kiến thức sâu rộng về]] the local area and its past. {{Moreover}}, I spent last summer working as a tour guide for a travel company, where I led groups of up to thirty people. This experience taught me how to [[speak confidently in public|nói trước đám đông một cách tự tin]] and [[deal with unexpected questions|xử lý những câu hỏi bất ngờ]]. I also speak fluent French, which might be useful for foreign visitors.

<<Ý 3>> My lectures finish on Fridays, {{so}} I would be available to work every Saturday and Sunday. I could also [[attend an interview|tham dự phỏng vấn]] on any weekday afternoon.

<<Kết thư>> I have enclosed my CV and [[look forward to hearing from you|mong nhận được hồi âm của quý vị]].

Yours faithfully,
Minh Tran
